items_missed: No pricing delivered on the call - no hourly rate, no what's-included list, no packing service pricing, despite the customer explicitly saying 'I would like to get a quote for that to see if I can afford it'
No No Worries Damage Coverage explanation
No 'no hidden fees' pitch and no 'pricing is super simple' opener
No clock explanation - clock start, 2.5 hour minimum, 15-minute increments, sense-check all absent
No estimate at all - no typical time range for a 1500 sqft one-story, no number of movers or trucks
No packing time explained even though full packing was the customer's central question
Glass-top patio table and king bed never addressed as specialty/disassembly items
Save Your Ass prep speech entirely absent
Never asked about long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns, parking, or HOA restrictions
Never said 'how are you today?' and gave no agenda statement or 'sound good?' confirmation

Walked away from the deal after one objection - 'Would that be a deal breaker for you?' then immediately conceded, with no attempt to salvage the movable portion (the house-to-house move) separately from the pod loading, and no referral offered for the pod/storage piece (Sparefoot or otherwise)
No booking attempt, no 'no deposit required', no 'any other questions before I let you go?', no hours or contact info given verbally
Used the customer's name only once, at goodbye ('have a good one Jess')
top_strength: Strong, efficient discovery for a 5.7 minute call - Amy confirmed both addresses, square footage, one-story status at both ends, additional stops, garage/shed/patio contents, and packing scope, and she proactively turned the one-mile distance into a selling point ('it's a super short drive... another good factor').
coaching_note: Amy lost a live, ready-to-buy customer the moment she hit the pod-loading limitation and never tried to save the rest of the job. The house-to-house move and the full packing service were both still sellable - the coaching is to separate what Einstein can't do from what it can, quote the part it can do, and hand off a referral for the rest instead of ending on 'totally understandable'.
phone_presence_notes: Some genuine warmth and an attempted rapport moment ('Wow, you're going on a trip. That's nice', 'Totally understandable'), but no opening pleasantry, near-zero name use, and the tone flattened into concession as soon as the customer pushed back.
